result.title: SCAP: Stochastic Context for Action Expert Pretraining
result.summary: Single-modality action-expert pretraining controls competition from visual shortcuts before vision--language--action (VLA) adaptation. Yet single-modality pretraining can impair the vision--language interactions needed for subsequent joint prediction. We construct a diagnostic model in which VA or LA pretraining can disable an initially active pathway for joint vision--language modeling. In this model, subsequent training with complete visual and language inputs cannot restore the pathway, even with unlimited adaptation. We therefore introduce Stochastic Context for Action Expert Pretraining (SCAP), a new action-expert pretraining stage that precedes full-input training. During this stage, visual and text tokens are randomly masked before entering the VLM. In this unified diagnostic model, SCAP can preserve the joint vision--language modeling pathway during pretraining and subsequent full-input training. Compared with direct full-input training, it can also reduce reliance on visual shortcuts and increase reliance on language instructions. SCAP consistently improves performance across four different VLA architectures. In real-robot experiments, it achieves 76.67% average success across three instruction-conditioned manipulation tasks, outperforming full-input pretraining by 25 percentage points.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 VLA 动作专家的预训练方式：先构建诊断模型说明单模态（VA 或 LA）预训练会使视觉-语言联合建模通路失活且不可恢复，进而提出 SCAP，在预训练阶段随机掩码视觉与文本 token，以保留联合通路、降低对视觉捷径的依赖并提升指令依从性，在多种 VLA 架构和真机操作任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单模态预训练使联合视觉-语言通路永久失活、随机掩码可保留该通路并削弱视觉捷径」的机制，可能为 VLM 推理中视觉旁路与信息坍缩的成因及训练期缓解提供可核查线索；但论文面向机器人动作专家，不涉及 latent 推理状态。
